{"self_assessment": "Impact: I chose the animal and drew the plan. A left-facing fish with a forked tail has a clear outline and a recognisable tail. I sketched it on the pad in the first minute, so the whole table could start building at once. I laid the start and the full top line of the body, which is the long upper outline and the backbone of the picture. I also laid the connect at the tail crossing, which brought more of the body into the run. At the push, about 199 of the 248 standing dominoes were connected to the start. I can't say whether the judge recognised the fish.

Execution: I kept my own stroke moving steadily from start to finish, then switched to checking the work. I inspected the nose, crossing and notch repeatedly and reported what I found. For example, I spotted the two open ends in the notch (one pointing left, one down-left) and told Maya which to join. I cleared a stray bit under the body and lifted two strays past the tail. That returned dominoes to the pile when supply ran short and kept the fall path clean.

Collaboration: I split the fish into clear pieces and assigned them by name: top line, bottom line and the two tail pieces. I kept the table updated and answered Tom, Leo and Maya directly. I stayed off the notch while Maya worked there, so we didn't bump each other. I passed on spare dominoes and told her when they were in the pile.

Leadership: I set the concept and the division of labour at the start. I kept the team focused on what the push would actually knock over, not just on what was standing. In the last minutes I supported the person on the final join instead of crowding her.", "my_share_percent": 30}
